Round1 supplier-first exact current authored Statement checked after EMsupplier freeze: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used to invoke the published Sobolev completeness theorem through its Countable-Choice interface ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq(-L,L)^3$ be bounded and open for some $L>0$, and write $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with the norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H_0^1(\Omega):=W_0^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ in that norm ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). Then $H^1(\Omega)$ is complete, $H_0^1(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace and is complete, the $W^{1,2}$ quadratic norm is a Hilbert norm (its coordinate $L^2$ pairings satisfy the parallelogram law), and

$$\|v\|_{L^2}^2\le(2L)^2\|\partial_1v\|_{L^2}^2\le(2L)^2\|\nabla v\|_{L^2}^2\qquad\text{for every }v\in H_0^1(\Omega).$$

In particular $\|v\|_{L^2}\le2L\|\nabla v\|_{L^2}$ and the gradient norm is equivalent to the full $H^1$ norm on $H_0^1(\Omega)$. The argument needs neither a smooth domain nor a general boundary-trace theorem, and no choice beyond the completeness interface is used. Round1 supplier-first exact current authored Statement checked after EMsupplier freeze: Assume AC and Countable Choice carried by the variational and Sobolev suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega$ be a bounded smooth graph domain in $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), $\varepsilon>0$ constant and $J$ an open interval. Let the bulk datum $f$ be jointly smooth up to $\overline\Omega\times J$ in the all-mixed-derivative sense of the parameter-preserving extension supplier, and let boundary families $g_D,\kappa$ be smooth in a fixed finite boundary atlas $\times\,J$. Then the Dirichlet problem $-\varepsilon\Delta u=f$, $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g_D$ has a unique solution on $\Omega\times J$; it has a single smooth ambient continuation near the closed spatial domain $\times\,J$. The Neumann problem $-\varepsilon\Delta u=f$, $\varepsilon\partial_\nu u=\kappa$ has such a solution precisely when

$$\int_{\Omega_j}f(\cdot,t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=0\quad\text{for each component and every }t\in J.$$

It is unique modulo a separately chosen spatial constant on each component at each time. The normalization $\int_{\Omega_j}u(\cdot,t)=0$ gives a unique smooth family. Both solution operations are linear in their data; time differentiation commutes with them. Smoothness and estimates are local in compact time subintervals, with no uniform-in-$J$ requirement.
